parameters.content:
## Bot Review · Outcomes (Phase 0)

Every 30 minutes: POST LP-MCP `/api/bot-feedback/jobs/outcomes`.

**What it does.** LP-MCP reconciles `bot_outcomes` for every fingerprinted bot send in the last 8 days that is not yet final — did the lead reply within 24h, did an appointment get created within 7 days, did they opt out within 24h. The signals are read from the HL cache and matched in code; LP and HL are never joined.

**Why a cron and not a webhook.** The three signals arrive on their own schedule (an inbound now, a booking on Thursday), so the only way to catch them is to look again. 30 minutes is the handoff's cadence (§5.1) and keeps a reply's outcome fresh enough for a same-day review.

**A 200 with `ok: false` is not a failure.** LP-MCP answers 200 for conditions that need a human — SQL not applied, `HL_SUPABASE_URL` unset — so the cron does not go red for something it cannot fix. Read `data.reason`. A red execution means LP-MCP was unreachable or threw.

**Stale HL cache is handled, not failed.** If HL messages or appointments last synced more than 2h ago, outcomes are still computed but recorded `source_fresh: false` and NEVER marked final, so a quiet cache is never mistaken for a quiet lead. Watch `data.source_fresh` in the execution output.

**Credential.** `LP MCP Bearer Auth` (Bearer Auth, value = LP-MCP's `MCP_AUTH_TOKEN`), pinned in this file BY ID. Naming it without an id made n8n bind this node to an unrelated bearer credential on the first import. If the credential is ever recreated, update its id here — `nodes` are pushed wholesale on every deploy, so a stale id clears the binding.

**Note on auth today.** LP-MCP runs with `AUTH_SOFT_LAUNCH` on, so `/api/bot-feedback/*` currently answers unauthenticated requests too. The token is therefore not yet load-bearing — but it will be the moment soft launch is turned off, which is why it is attached now.

nodes.name: Every 30 min ET
nodes.notes: Every 30 minutes, around the clock. Timezone America/New_York is set on the workflow so this and every other Bot Review cron share the business clock (handoff §0/§6); for a fixed half-hourly interval the zone makes no difference to the firing times, but it does to how the executions read.

nodes.name: POST outcomes job
nodes.notes:
120s timeout: one run reconciles up to BOT_OUTCOMES_BATCH_LIMIT (500) fingerprints and makes three batched HL reads. neverError is left at its default (false) — there is no repair branch to route a non-2xx into, so a genuine LP-MCP failure should fail the execution and be visible in the execution list. The soft conditions (SQL not applied, HL credentials unset) come back as 200 with ok:false and do not go red.

CREDENTIAL IS PINNED BY ID, not by name. The first cut of this file named it without an id; n8n could not match it and silently bound the node to an unrelated httpBearerAuth credential instead ("Supabase Highlevel MCP"), which would have sent the HL Supabase service key to LP-MCP on every run. The id is what makes the binding deterministic. This file's `nodes` are pushed wholesale on every deploy, so if the credential is ever recreated its new id must be updated here or the next deploy will clear the binding.

meta.note: Bot Review Phase 0 (handoff §6). Requires LP-MCP to expose POST /api/bot-feedback/jobs/outcomes, which ships in the LP-MCP Phase 0 PR. Shipped INACTIVE: activate only after sql/103_bot_feedback_core.sql is applied and LP-MCP is deployed, or every run returns ok:false with reason 'missing_relation'.
